PRODUCTION-CHANGE GATE (Git #1913): the boundary is the app registration, not the tenant - mccawsoft2.onmicrosoft.com is both the testbed and the real production Microsoft 365 tenant, so testbed only is a real constraint for reads and none at all for writes. DEV app registration 9f6f4772-b5be-421f-815e-b392336c373a, ca-ps-execution-dev, and reads against the testbed tenant are agent-modifiable with no gate. PROD app registration 3308b280-e41e-42ba-9f73-73aac2ad3dee, production Key Vault ShaneMcCawConsulting secrets, ca-ps-execution (the non-dev container), and Staging/Replit deploys and their migrations are never applied by an agent - read state and write the plan, then hand it to #1281 (GATE: v1.1 release) instead of applying it yourself. PNPM INSTALL IS NOT A REMEDY (Git #1987): never prescribe pnpm install to fix broken module resolution, in code, logs, commits, or chat - on an unchanged lockfile pnpm exits without walking any symlinks, so a link dangling into a deleted worktree survives every run; diagnose the actual link instead (dir on Windows, or fsutil reparsepoint query for junctions) and file what you find as a worktree isolation bug, not a dependency problem. pnpm install --force is prohibited - it refetches roughly 1120 packages, a real metered cost on a capped connection, and does not repair a dangling link. Never run pnpm install from inside a worktree; use scripts/dev-server/link-deps.mjs junctions instead. Bandwidth is a real constraint you cannot infer - treat any large download as a cost needing justification. If a metered or blocked operation is hit, stop and report it plainly: do not retry it, do not go looking for an alternate command that achieves the same download, and do not write to settings yourself to clear the block. The override belongs to Shane, taken in BuildConsole, and is one shot. BLOCKED_BY EDGES ARE THE GATE (Git #1987): when you conclude an issue cannot proceed, make that machine readable in the same action, not only a comment - file the real blocker as its own issue if it is not one already, wire a blocked_by dependency edge to it, and remove any stale blocked_by edge that no longer reflects reality, especially one pointing at an issue that is closed or about to close, since a closing blocker silently releases everything downstream.
